<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is an open‑source, frontend JavaScript library (“Frappe Gantt”) for rendering customizable Gantt charts in the browser. It’s not a full‑stack app but a component library that provides an embeddable Gantt chart widget.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top‑level:  
     • src/ – core source modules (arrow.js, bar.js, date_utils.js, popup.js, svg_utils.js, defaults.js, index.js)  
     • styles under src/styles – three theme CSS files  
     • builder/ – a small demo harness (demo.js, demo.css) used to showcase the library  
     • tests/ – unit tests for utility functions  
     • index.html, vite.config.js, package.json, build and config files – build, packaging, CI (publish.yml)

3. Key insights from README  
   - The library exports a Gantt class (`new Gantt(...)`) that takes a container selector and an array of tasks.  
   - It’s built to be framework‑agnostic (vanilla JS + CSS + SVG).  
   - It supports rich configuration (view modes, popups, dependency arrows, holidays, localization).

4. Main components for your system diagram  
   a. Core Modules (in src/):  
      - Gantt Class (index.js) – orchestrator, public API  
      - Bar Renderer (bar.js) – draws task bars  
      - Arrow Renderer (arrow.js) – draws dependency arrows  
      - SVG Utilities (svg_utils.js) – helper for SVG element creation/manipulation  
      - Date Utilities (date_utils.js) – date math (intervals, diff, formatting)  
      - Popup Manager (popup.js) – event handling + dynamic popup generation  
      - Defaults & Configuration (defaults.js) – default options & override logic  
      - CSS Themes (dark.css, light.css, gantt.css) – styling layers  
   b. Build & Packaging  
      - Vite (vite.config.js) – bundles and outputs ESM and UMD artifacts  
      - builder/ – demo harness showing integration example  
      - CI/CD (publish.yml) – on‑push publishing to npm/CDN  
   c. Tests  
      - date_utils.test.js – ensures time calculations are correct  

5. Relationships and interactions  
   - At runtime, the consumer’s code calls `new Gantt(...)` → Gantt Class loads defaults → parses tasks via Date Utilities → renders SVG container via SVG Utilities → iterates over tasks: uses Bar Renderer & Arrow Renderer → attaches event listeners for drag/drop and popups via Popup Manager  
   - Build pipeline: src/ → Vite → dist/frappe-gantt.umd.js + dist/frappe-gantt.esm.js + CSS → published to npm or CDN  
   - Demo harness: index.html + builder/demo.js/css imports the distributed bundle to illustrate usage  

6. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Modular design: each renderer and utility is encapsulated in its own module  
   - Single Responsibility: date logic, rendering logic, popup logic separated  
   - Plugin‑style configuration: defaults.js merges with user options to customize behavior  
   - Build‑time bundling for universal module definition (UMD) and ESM  

7. Tailoring your diagram for this open‑source library  
   - Emphasize core library modules as distinct boxes (use one color for rendering modules, another for utilities, a third for configuration)  
   - Show the consumer boundary: how a web page (index.html or demo) imports the UMD/ESM bundle  
   - Illustrate the build pipeline separately: Vite transforms src → dist → publish  
   - Highlight extension points: the `popup` function hook, custom `view_modes`, theme CSS overrides  

8. Diagram elements & guidelines  
   - Components: Label boxes for “Gantt Class”, “Bar Renderer”, “Arrow Renderer”, “Date Utils”, “SVG Utils”, “Popup Manager”, “Defaults/Config”, “CSS Themes”, “Build Pipeline”, “Demo Harness”, “Test Suite”, “CI/CD”  
   - Arrows:  
     • Solid arrows for “runtime data flow” (Gantt → Bar/Arrow → SVG Utils → DOM)  
     • Dashed arrows for “build flow” (src → Vite → dist → publish)  
     • Double‑headed arrows for “configuration merge” (Defaults ↔ User Options)  
   - Color‐coding or shapes:  
     • Green boxes for core rendering modules  
     • Blue boxes for utilities  
     • Yellow boxes for build & CI  
     • Grey boxes for demo & tests  
   - Directional flow: left‑to‑right for build pipeline; top‑to‑bottom for runtime flow inside browser  

9. Detailed steps for drawing  
   1. Place “Source Modules (src/)” cluster on left, subdivided into Rendering, Utilities, Config  
   2. To the right, show “Build Tool (Vite)” → “Distribution (dist/.js, .css)” → “Publish (npm/CDN)”  
   3. Below, show “Demo Harness (builder/)” and “User Web Page (index.html)” both consuming Distribution  
   4. From “User Web Page”, draw arrow into “Runtime Flow” area: → “Gantt Class” → branches to Bar/Arrow Renderers, Date Utils, Popup Manager → DOM (SVG Container + CSS Themes)  
   5. Off to one side, show “Tests (tests/)” pointing at Date Utils  
   6. At top, show “CI/CD (.github/workflows)” overseeing Build & Publish  

By following this layout and these conventions, you’ll produce a clear, accurate system design diagram that captures Frappe Gantt’s architecture, build process, and integration story.  
</explanation>
